title: Federated learning for computational pathology on gigapixel whole slide images
authors: Lu MY; Chen RJ; Kong D; Lipkova J; Singh R; Williamson DFK; Chen TY; Mahmood F
summary: Federated attention-based multiple-instance learning on gigapixel slides, with Gaussian-noise differential privacy, tested on breast and kidney subtyping and kidney survival using three simulated sites cut from TCGA tissue-source sites. Federated AUC fell below centralised training (breast subtyping about 0.86 vs 0.92; kidney subtyping about 0.976 vs 0.985) but exceeded single-site models, and communication pace (1 to 8 local epochs) changed little.
note: arXiv 2009.10190 is the preprint; sites are simulated, not real institutions; each round sends the full MIL model weights.

title: Swarm learning for decentralized artificial intelligence in cancer histopathology
authors: Saldanha OL; Quirke P; West NP; James JA; Loughrey MB; Grabsch HI; Salto-Tellez M; Alwers E; Cifci D; Ghaffari Laleh N; Seibel T; Gray R; Hutchins GGA; Brenner H; van Treeck M; Yuan T; Brinker TJ; Chang-Claude J; Khader F; Schuppert A; Luedde T; Trautwein C; Muti HS; Foersch S; Hoffmeister M; Truhn D; Kather JN
summary: Swarm learning (peer-to-peer weight averaging, blockchain-coordinated) across three colorectal cohorts (Northern Ireland, Germany, US; over 5,000 patients) to predict BRAF and MSI status from H&E slides. Swarm models beat most local models and matched a merged-data model (QUASAR MSI AUROC 0.8326 vs 0.8308 merged), and held up when each site was cut to 100-400 patients.
note: Real multi-country physical sites; training an attention-MIL head on frozen-encoder tile features, many rounds.

title: Federated learning and differential privacy for medical image analysis
authors: Adnan M; Kalra S; Cresswell JC; Taylor GW; Tizhoosh HR
summary: Differentially private federated learning (DP-SGD) for lung cancer histopathology classification, simulating hospitals from TCGA tissue-source sites, with external validation. At epsilon 2.90 (delta 1e-4) test accuracy was 0.823 for DP-FL and FL against 0.839 pooled; external accuracy was 0.707 (DP-FL), 0.741 (FL) and 0.768 (pooled), against 0.56-0.70 for single-site training.
note: Simulated sites; gives a concrete accuracy cost of DP in an image-classification federation.

title: Proportionally Fair Hospital Collaborations in Federated Learning of Histopathology Images
authors: Hosseini SM; Sikaroudi M; Babaie M; Tizhoosh HR
summary: Proposes Prop-FFL, a federated objective that narrows the spread of performance across hospitals, tested on two histopathology datasets and two general datasets. Reports gains in learning speed, accuracy and fairness over comparison schemes.
note: Seed. Full text not read; the lead should read it only if per-site fairness matters.

title: Flexible and scalable federated learning with deep feature prompts for digital pathology
authors: Cong C; Song Y; Di Ieva A; Chou A; J Gill A; Coiera E; Liu S
summary: Federated Deep Feature Prompting: clients keep a pretrained patch encoder and a local MIL model frozen and share only small learnable prompts applied to patch embeddings of whole-slide images. On TCGA-IDH, CAMELYON16 and CAMELYON17 it gains 0.11-0.13 mean AUC over local-only training and up to 0.10 over the best federated baseline while exchanging about 1K parameters (single-digit KB) per round against 0.8M or 24M for others.
note: Closest published match to routes 2-3 on frozen features, but iterative (rounds) and for slide-level classification, not expression. Research Square preprint rs-7060589 also exists.

title: FedSDA: Federated Stain Distribution Alignment for Non-IID Histopathological Image Classification
authors: Cheng-Chang Tsai; Kai-Wen Cheng; Chun-Shien Lu
summary: Aligns stain distributions across federated clients with a diffusion model trained on stain matrices rather than raw images, to reduce non-IID shift in histopathology classification. Reports gains over update-side and data-side non-IID baselines.
note: Seed (AAAI 2026, 40(12):9566-9575, ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/37918, seen via web search). Full PDF saved, not read in detail.

title: The future of digital health with federated learning
authors: Rieke N; Hancox J; Li W; Milletarì F; Roth HR; Albarqouni S; Bakas S; Galtier MN; Landman BA; Maier-Hein K; Ourselin S; Sheller M; Summers RM; Trask A; Xu D; Baust M; Cardoso MJ
summary: Perspective by an FL consortium on how federated learning may unlock siloed medical data, covering architectures, privacy, bias and governance considerations. A standard reference for what leaves a site (parameters, gradients) and the technical and regulatory issues.
note: arXiv 2003.08119 is the preprint. Federated learning review; privacy section notes face reconstruction from CT/MRI and model memorisation, and names differential privacy and encrypted learning as additions. Full text read in targeted passages (abstract, methods/results, discussion), not line by line.

title: Swarm Learning for decentralized and confidential clinical machine learning
authors: Warnat-Herresthal S; Schultze H; Shastry KL; Manamohan S; Mukherjee S; Garg V; Sarveswara R; Händler K; Pickkers P; Aziz NA; Ktena S; Tran F; Bitzer M; Ossowski S; Casadei N; Herr C; Petersheim D; Behrends U; Kern F; Fehlmann T; Schommers P; Lehmann C; Augustin M; Rybniker J; Altmüller J; Mishra N; Mishra N; Bernardes JP; Krämer B; Bonaguro L; Schulte-Schrepping J; De Domenico E; Siever C; Kraut M; Desai M; Monnet B; Saridaki M; Siegel CM; Drews A; Nuesch-Germano M; Theis H; Heyckendorf J; Schreiber S; Kim-Hellmuth S; COVID-19 Aachen Study (COVAS); Nattermann J; Skowasch D; Kurth I; Keller A; Bals R; Nürnberg P; Rieß O; Rosenstiel P; Netea MG; Theis F; Mukherjee S; Backes M; Aschenbrenner AC; Ulas T; Deutsche COVID-19 Omics Initiative (DeCOI); Breteler MMB; Giamarellos-Bourboulis EJ; Kox M; Becker M; Cheran S; Woodacre MS; Goh EL; Schultze JL

note: Includes expression data (blood RNA), so relevant to Q5 for omics federations; not histology. Swarm learning with permissioned blockchain and no central coordinator; transcriptomic (127 studies) and >95,000 chest X-ray data; swarm classifiers outperformed single-site ones in the paper's words. Not histology. Full text read in targeted passages (abstract, methods/results, discussion), not line by line.

title: PPML-Omics: A privacy-preserving federated machine learning method protects patients' privacy in omic data
authors: Zhou J; Chen S; Wu Y; Li H; Zhang B; Zhou L; Hu Y; Xiang Z; Li Z; Chen N; Han W; Xu C; Wang D; Gao X
summary: PPML-Omics: decentralised differentially private federated learning applied to bulk RNA-seq cancer classification, scRNA-seq clustering and ST-Net prediction of spatial expression from H&E on spatial transcriptomics, with gradient-inversion attacks tested on each. It reports utility at or above comparison methods at the same privacy level and that DP blocked the attacks, but this record gives no cross-site accuracy-loss curve for the ST-Net task.
note: Published Sci Adv 2024;10(5):eadh8601 (read at abstract level); full text read is the bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2022.03.23.485485 (v1 and v2), whose text differs from the published version. Sites are simulated. Only federated expression-from-H&E paper found.

title: A review on federated learning in computational pathology
authors: Schoenpflug LA; Nie Y; Sheikhzadeh F; Koelzer VH
summary: Survey of 15 federated-learning studies in computational pathology. Reports federated models on par with or 0.2-6% below centralised ones, domain-alignment methods giving larger gains (4-20%) than aggregation tweaks (0-3%), and calls for deployment guidelines.
note: Review; full text saved, only abstract read. Practical-guide review of FL in computational pathology; its privacy section summarises DP (about -6% accuracy in one cited comparison) vs SMC (about -0.5%) and notes that most studies do not measure privacy loss. Full text read in targeted passages (abstract, methods/results, discussion), not line by line.

title: Navigating real-world challenges: A case study on federated learning in computational pathology
authors: Schoenpflug LA; Bagan Benavides R; Nowak M; Sheikhzadeh F; Moayyedi A; Wasag K; Reimers J; Zhou M; Venugopal R; TumorProfiler Consortium; Sobottka B; Koeller Y; Rivers M; Moch H; Nie Y; Koelzer VH
summary: Account of running a real federation with NVIDIA FLARE for immune phenotyping in metastatic melanoma: three clients and a central server on four separate networks in four countries. Documents practical obstacles (firewalls, hosting the server on a semi-public AWS network, GPU needs and IT expertise).
note: Real-deployment evidence for governance and site compute requirements; read the Methods/abstract text, not every section.

title: Nationwide federated learning for histopathology: secure deployment across Germany behind firewalls
authors: Babendererde N; Lemke N; Stieber J; Fuchs M; Weng Z; Eich ML; Lingscheidt T; Mairinger F; Büttner R; Tolkach Y; Mukhopadhyay A
summary: TheODen, a federation platform deployed across German hospitals behind firewalls without opening inbound ports, for histopathology segmentation. Global Dice was 0.764 on BCSS and 0.754 on SemiCOL despite data heterogeneity and network limits.
note: Number of live hospital sites not extracted from the text I searched; lead should check. Practice evidence for analysis running at the data home.

title: Comparing decentralized machine learning and AI clinical models to local and centralized alternatives: a systematic review
authors: Diniz JM; Vasconcelos H; Rb-Silva R; Ameijeiras-Rodriguez C; Rodrigues D; Ramos P; Tomás A; Gao Y; Souza J; Freitas A
summary: Systematic review of decentralised learning (federated, swarm, ensemble) in healthcare, screening 165,010 records. Decentralised models were typically within about 0.7-1.5 percentage points of centralised ones and far better than local-only models (7.6-27 points).
note: Cross-domain, not histology-specific; summary numbers from the abstract. Systematic review: 160 articles, 710 DL models, 8,149 comparisons; includes a table of pathology/WSI studies. Only skimmed the pathology rows; comparison-direction statistics not extracted. Full text read in targeted passages (abstract, methods/results, discussion), not line by line.

title: FedDBL: Communication and Data Efficient Federated Deep-Broad Learning for Histopathological Tissue Classification
authors: Tianpeng Deng; Yanqi Huang; Guoqiang Han; Zhenwei Shi; Jiatai Lin; Qi Dou; Zaiyi Liu; Xiao-jing Guo; C. L. Philip Chen; Chu Han
summary: FedDBL fits a broad-learning (closed-form linear) head on frozen CNN or pathology-pretrained features in one communication round for histopathological tile classification. Matching multi-round federated learning, it cuts communication from 4.6 GB to 276.5 KB per client (ResNet-50), and with one round and 100% data it approaches centralised MCC (R-Centralized 0.938 on MC-CRC).
note: Nearest published analogue of C1 (frozen features, one round, closed form); classification not regression; published in a journal (PMID 38923486 lists it in 2024) but opened as arXiv.

title: Pseudo-Data Based Self-Supervised Federated Learning for Classification of Histopathological Images
authors: Zhang Y; Li Z; Han X; Ding S; Li J; Wang J; Ying S; Shi J
summary: Self-supervised pretraining of a shared backbone on pseudo-images generated at each centre, followed by Barlow-Twins-based federated training for histopathology classification. Reported improved accuracy and generalisation on four public datasets.
note: Route 4 (federated SSL) precedent, but shares synthetic images, not weights; arXiv 2205.15530.

title: Probing the Efficacy of Federated Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Vision Transformers for Medical Image Classification
authors: Naif Alkhunaizi; Faris Almalik; Rouqaiah Al-Refai; Muzammal Naseer; Karthik Nandakumar
summary: Benchmark of federated parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) of vision transformers for medical image classification, including out-of-domain transfer. Reports that each ten-fold cut in exchanged parameters costs about 4% accuracy and that an in-domain medical foundation model is the better start.
note: Preprint; evidence for route 3 trade-offs. Concludes PEFT methods have limited efficacy on heterogeneous or out-of-domain datasets; ViT pretrained on natural images, medical image classification. Full text read in targeted passages (abstract, methods/results, discussion), not line by line.

title: A Federated Learning-Friendly Approach for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of SAM in 3D Segmentation
authors: Mothilal Asokan; Joseph Geo Benjamin; Mohammad Yaqub; Karthik Nandakumar
summary: Federated LoRA adaptation of the Segment Anything Model for 3D medical segmentation, choosing which layers to federate. On Fed-KiTS it cuts communication about 48x versus full fine-tuning while raising Dice by about 6%.
note: Preprint; radiology; route 3.

title: Personalized Federated Fine-Tuning of Vision Foundation Models for Healthcare
authors: Adam Tupper; Christian Gagné
summary: Personalised federated fine-tuning with orthogonal LoRA adapters that separate shared from client-specific knowledge. Preliminary results on real federated medical imaging tasks are competitive with other federated fine-tuning methods.
note: Preprint, preliminary.

title: FedMM: Federated Multi-Modal Learning with Modality Heterogeneity in Computational Pathology
authors: Yuanzhe Peng; Jieming Bian; Jie Xu
summary: FedMM federates single-modality feature extractors across hospitals with different modality sets in computational pathology. It beats two baselines in accuracy and AUC on two public datasets.
note: Preprint.

title: Federated Stain Normalization for Computational Pathology
authors: Nicolas Wagner; Moritz Fuchs; Yuri Tolkach; Anirban Mukhopadhyay
summary: BottleGAN learns stain mappings across laboratories in a privacy-preserving federated way to align appearance. It raises IoU by 42% over existing federated algorithms on a heterogeneous PESO-based dataset.
note: Preprint; relevant to lab/stain heterogeneity across centres.

title: Federated learning with hyper-network-a case study on whole slide image analysis
authors: Lin Y; Wang H; Li W; Shen J
summary: A hypernetwork on the server generates client MIL classifier weights, with noise added to the exchanged parameters, for whole-slide classification on TCGA sites. It beats isolated sites and FedAvg (TCGA-NSCLC AUC 0.920 vs 0.912 for FedAvg).
note: Numbers from the web-search page of the paper; sites simulated from TCGA.

title: Federated CT foundation models for multi-center detection of lymph node metastasis in pancreatic cancer
authors: Bhalla P; Gaviria DD; Kupczyk P; Hosseini ASA; Conradi L; Fehrenbach U; Felsenstein M; Ma D; Semaan A; Albarqouni S
summary: Combines a CT foundation model with a heterogeneity-aware federated strategy for lymph-node metastasis detection in pancreatic cancer. It recovers much of the centralised model performance and improves balanced accuracy by 12.6% over FedAvg.
note: Radiology; route 3-4 evidence with a foundation model.

title: Federated generative prompt learning with vision foundation models: universal efficient multi-center medical image analysis
authors: Lin X; Chen Y; Wu J; Xu C; Li J; Su X
summary: Federated generative prompt learning with frozen vision foundation models (ViT, SAM): only 8.26% and 6.55% of parameters are trained and convergence takes 15 rounds. It beats full fine-tuning and keeps performance with 5% of the training data.
note: Route 3 on foundation models in non-pathology imaging.

title: Federated Foundation Model for GI Endoscopy Images
authors: Alina Devkota; Annahita Amireskandari; Joel Palko; Shyam Thakkar; Donald Adjeroh; Xiajun Jiang; Binod Bhattarai; Prashnna K. Gyawali
summary: Trains a gastrointestinal-endoscopy foundation model by federated self-supervised pretraining and fine-tunes it on classification, detection and segmentation. Reports improved downstream performance in homogeneous and heterogeneous settings.
note: Route 4 precedent outside pathology; preprint.

title: Privacy-Preserving Surgical Video Analysis with Swarm Learning - Results from a Multinational Appendectomy Cohort
authors: Saldanha OL; Pfeiffer K; Bodenstedt S; Kirchner M; Jenke AC; Barata C; Barbosa S; Barthel J; Carstens M; Castro LT; Dehlke K; Dietz S; Emmanouilidis S; Fitze G; Holderried F; Kanjo W; Leitermann L; Mees ST; Soares AS; Pascoal M; Pistorius S; Prudlo C; Schultz J; Seiberth A; Thiel K; Wu X; Ziehn D; Speidel S; Weitz J; Distler M; Kather JN; Kolbinger FR
summary: Swarm learning for predicting patient-level grading from laparoscopic surgery video across institutions (appendicitis), with a user survey on deployment. Performance was on par with centralised learning; hardware failures and poor EHR integration were the main obstacles.
note: Practice evidence on deployment barriers; linked to FedSurg.

title: Federated Learning in Healthcare: From Research to Real-World Deployment
authors: Bakas S; Li X; Shah P; Roth HR
summary: Review of federated learning in healthcare from research to deployment, covering non-IID handling, differential privacy, secure aggregation and confidential computing, and FL-as-a-service. Argues for interoperable infrastructure and regulation-aligned workflows.
note: Review.

title: Do Gradient Inversion Attacks Make Federated Learning Unsafe?
authors: Hatamizadeh A; Yin H; Molchanov P; Myronenko A; Li W; Dogra P; Feng A; Flores MG; Kautz J; Xu D; Roth HR
summary: Shows that published gradient-inversion attacks fail when clients update batch-normalisation statistics and offers a new baseline attack for that case, plus ways to measure leakage. Frames the tradeoff between differential privacy and accuracy as something to measure by leakage.
note: Opened via Europe PMC record; DOI 10.1109/TMI.2023.3239391. Read the arXiv version (2202.06924) of the paper; text states gradient-inversion attacks in the literature assume fixed batch-norm statistics and are impractical when BN statistics are updated. Full text read in targeted passages (abstract, methods/results, discussion), not line by line.

title: Re-identification from histopathology images
authors: Ganz J; Ammeling J; Jabari S; Breininger K; Aubreville M
summary: Shows that deep learning can match a whole-slide image to its source patient among other slides of the same cohort. The arXiv version reports F1 of 50.16% (TCGA LSCC), 52.30% (LUAD) and 62.31% (in-house meningioma); the published abstract reports higher values (up to 80.1% on TCGA lung squamous, 77.2% and 77.1% on the other two). Proposes a risk assessment for sharing slides.
note: Full text read = arXiv version (2403.12816, fetched via Unpaywall; saved in papers folder). The published MedIA text itself was not read, so the version difference is unresolved: always state which version a number comes from. Published: Med Image Anal 2025, DOI 10.1016/j.media.2024.103335.

title: Encrypted federated learning for secure decentralized collaboration in cancer image analysis
authors: Truhn D; Tayebi Arasteh S; Saldanha OL; Müller-Franzes G; Khader F; Quirke P; West NP; Gray R; Hutchins GGA; James JA; Loughrey MB; Salto-Tellez M; Brenner H; Brobeil A; Yuan T; Chang-Claude J; Hoffmeister M; Foersch S; Han T; Keil S; Schulze-Hagen M; Isfort P; Bruners P; Kaissis G; Kuhl C; Nebelung S; Kather JN
summary: Homomorphically encrypted federated learning (SHEFL) on multicentre radiology and histopathology tasks, where only encrypted weights leave sites. Models beat local ones and matched centrally trained ones.
note: Cost of encryption not extracted.

title: A Dataset Auditing Method for Collaboratively Trained Machine Learning Models
authors: Huang Y; Huang CY; Li X; Li K
summary: Ensembled Membership Auditing combines membership-inference scores to test whether a given dataset was used to train a model in a federated setting. Evaluated on four X-ray and three dermatology datasets, it outperforms prior auditing methods.
note: Governance/enforcement angle.

title: Differentially private federated deep learning for multi-site medical image segmentation
authors: Alexander Ziller; Dmitrii Usynin; Nicolas Remerscheid; Moritz Knolle; Marcus Makowski; Rickmer Braren; Daniel Rueckert; Georgios Kaissis
summary: Differentially private federated segmentation of CT images, with the first gradient-based model inversion attack shown on a segmentation model. High segmentation quality is possible under strong privacy guarantees at a training-time cost, and DP prevents the inversion.
note: Preprint.

title: Siloed Federated Learning for Multi-Centric Histopathology Datasets
authors: Mathieu Andreux; Jean Ogier du Terrail; Constance Beguier; Eric W. Tramel
summary: Local-statistic batch-norm layers give center-specific models in a federated histopathology setting and avoid sharing activation statistics. Compares favourably on Camelyon16/17, especially for transfer across datasets.
note: Preprint; shows center-specific parameters (cf. center-specific intercepts in C1).

title: Federated Learning for surgical vision in appendicitis classification: Results of the FedSurg EndoVis 2024 challenge
authors: Kirchner M; Hoffmann H; Jenke AC; Saldanha OL; Pfeiffer K; Kanjo W; Alekseenko J; de Boer C; Kolamuri SR; Mazza L; Padoy N; Bano S; Reinke A; Maier-Hein L; Stoyanov D; Kather JN; Kolbinger FR; Bodenstedt S; Speidel S
summary: FedSurg Challenge benchmarking federated learning for appendicitis grading from surgical video across centres. Performance stayed poor even with pooled data (F1 26.31% on the unseen centre) and no adaptation comparison reached significance at this sample size.
note: Honest negative-ish benchmark; shows evaluation limits at small scale.

title: FairFedMed: Benchmarking Group Fairness in Federated Medical Imaging With FairLoRA
authors: Li M; Wen C; Tian Y; Shi M; Luo Y; Huang H; Fang Y; Wang M
summary: Benchmark for group fairness in federated medical imaging with FairLoRA, an SVD-based low-rank approach. Reports state-of-the-art classification and better fairness across demographic groups.
note: Marginal; route 3 (LoRA).

title: Federated Learning: A new frontier in the exploration of multi-institutional medical imaging data
authors: Dominika Ciupek; Maciej Malawski; Tomasz Pieciak
summary: Survey of federated learning for multi-institutional medical imaging: aggregation and learning algorithms, data and model heterogeneity, privacy attacks, frameworks and real implementations.
